title: synchronize-cred-retry-profiles-and-stream-surface-for-py-ts-go
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: Three SDK teams have drifted on small-but-cumulative differences in auth windowing, retry presets, and streaming consumer ergonomics which cause intermittent resume failures and inconsistent telemetry. This PR harmonizes behavior across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs: 1) introduces a shared retry-profile artifact (lightweight JSON schema) and per-transport tuning hooks, 2) aligns the streaming async iterator/pullstream surface so all SDKs expose a pause/resume-friendly API (named StreamHandle in TS/Go and StreamSession in Python) with consistent backpressure hints, and 3) bumps SDK package versions to signal the ergonomics changes and minor breaking renames. Changes are additive where possible; a migration note is included for clients using raw internal session objects. Motivation: reduce cross-language surprises for platform users integrating with multi-service deployments and enable unified telemetry and experimentation of retry profiles. Summary of changes: - add /sdk/common/retry_profiles/schema.json and a small generator that emits language-specific presets - Python: add redispatch layer for retry presets, expose StreamSession.pause() and .resume(), docstrings and typed stubs updated - TypeScript: introduce StreamHandle with pause()/resume()/signalBackpressure(), migrate existing generator adapter to use new retry hook - Go: add RetryProfileLoader and StreamHandle type; ensure zero-allocation resume path for KV-cache hot path - tests: cross-sdk golden fixtures for backpressure signaling, end-to-end flaky-auth simulation harness - docs: migration guide under sdk/*/MIGRATING.md and cross-sdk examples under examples/streaming/multi-lang.md Testing and CI: unit tests for each SDK, cross-language e2e that runs a simulated auth rotation and intermittent 503s, linting and typechecks for all three SDKs passed. Release: bump py to 1.11.0, ts to 2.6.0, go to v1.9.0. Backwards compatibility: most surface additions are non-breaking; renames are documented and shims provided for a single minor release. Rollout plan: staged canary for hosted customers and library deprecation notices sent to heavy users.
